status: UNCONSTRAINED DESIGN SEARCH, shuttle v0.1 (canon set aside, physics kept). Every assumption is authored and visible. Not canon, not engineering.
brief: kT 2026-10-24: atmospheric landing including Venus pressures, aerobraking, a human-drivable rover aboard, and airless landings too.

venus_atmosphere.what: Venus T and P every 5 km to 100 km (VIRA); surface density 65 kg/m3

venera_9.what: parachute dropped at ~50 km, fell by drag alone, landed at ~7 m/s; worked 53 min

venus_sample_return_2024.what: surface launch 'almost impossibly difficult due to the density'; a high-temperature aircraft lifts the sample off the surface; rocket launches from a balloon at ~60-65 km; metal-bellows surface balloon 'an extremely difficult technology element'; orbit from 65 km nearly as hard as from Earth's surface

havoc.what: NASA crewed Venus airship at ~50 km: Earth-like pressure and temperature, breathable air is a lifting gas, sulfuric acid haze

venus_cooling.what: 24 h consumable cooling for a Venus lander: 18 kg NH3/He vented for 150 W at 92 bar

sic_electronics.what: SiC integrated circuit ran 21.7 days at 460 C and 93 atm in NASA GEER; SiC logic 4,000 h at 500 C

adept.what: deployable carbon-fabric heat shield (umbrella ribs); Venus target 250 W/cm2; ballistic coefficient <50 kg/m2 vs ~250 rigid; 6.5 m example aeroshell ~870 kg of 2,500 kg

hiad_applications.what: LOFTID 6 m, 1,100 kg, 8 km/s, 40 W/cm2; Gen-2 flexible TPS ~50 W/cm2; HIAD aerocapture cases at Mars and Earth with L/D 0.2

hiad_scaling.what: >36 t landed at Mars needs a 16-20 m HIAD

tps_correlation.what: Laub & Venkatapathy TPS mass fraction % = 0.091 Q^0.51575, Q = stagnation heat load in J/cm2 (over-predicts at high loads)

mars_ascent_vehicle.what: NASA MAV trades: 24.4 t storable SSTO to 500 km; LOX/CH4 two-stage 42.9-48.9 t; crew cabin 3.9-4.3 t for 4

delta_v_budget.what: Earth to LEO 9.3-10 km/s incl. 1.5-2 drag and gravity losses; Mars surface to low orbit 4.1; Moon surface to low orbit 1.87

sev.what: NASA Space Exploration Vehicle: 2 crew for 2 weeks, 4.5 m long, 3 m tall, ~3-4 t; the same cabin mounts on a wheeled chassis or an in-space flyer

direct_fusion_drive.what: small fusion drive concept that gives both thrust and electric power

canon_candidate.what: Wayfarer candidate spec: shuttle ~30-35 t lifting-body/VTOL; ground vehicle 2.7-3.0 x 1.5-1.7 x 1.3-1.5 m, 1.2-1.8 t

canon_atlas_venus.what: Venus is a cloud/orbital civilization (~1.8M); surface access is not the settlement norm

Mercury.note: dayside surface ~700 K; work near the terminator or at night

Callisto.note: stands in for the Galilean and other large airless moons

atm.source: authored two-layer fit to the Huygens-era profile (surface 1.47 bar, 94 K; tropopause ~44 km at ~0.1 bar, 70 K; stratospheric scale height ~30 km)

sutton_graves_k.note: q [W/m2] = k sqrt(rho/r_nose) v^3; convective only; radiative heating ignored (fair below ~8 km/s)

Venus clouds.note: dock at a cloud city and launch from it

job_rules.round_trip: every job starts and ends in the mothership's parking orbit, carrying crew and rover both ways
job_rules.note: margins and ratings are authored conceptual-design values

METHALOX.label: Methane/oxygen rocket
METHALOX.fuel_from: carbon needed: made at Mars, Venus (CO2) or Titan (methane); Wayfarer carries only water

TORCH.label: Fusion torchlet on water
notes: power-limited like Wayfarer's torch: lower exhaust speed buys thrust (5-20 km/s, authored)
pc_equiv: a ~10 T magnetic nozzle holds ~400 bar of plasma pressure; expansion against ambient air is lost (authored model)
1 GW of jet power per tonne is authored; Wayfarer's own torch implies far more, Discovery II far less
inherits Wayfarer's open torch heat-deposition question

PROPULSIVE.label: No heat shield (burn all the way down)

LIFTING_BODY.label: Lifting body, rigid tiles
LIFTING_BODY.precedent: Space Shuttle, HL-20, Dream Chaser, X-37B

DEPLOYABLE.label: Capsule body plus deployable umbrella shield (beta 100)
DEPLOYABLE.reusable: umbrella ribs re-stow (assumed for 2226); fabric replaced every few entries

entry.note: aspect_lwh: bounding-box proportions; fly_ld: lift-to-drag when flying slowly on fans in the low Venus atmosphere (1 = fans hold the weight)
entry.acreage_note: windward acreage of a lifting body sees a fraction of the nose heat load (authored from Shuttle-type heating distributions); capsules and umbrellas take the stagnation value

DEPLOYABLE_200.label: Capsule body plus deployable umbrella shield (beta 200)
DEPLOYABLE_200.reusable: umbrella ribs re-stow (assumed for 2226); fabric replaced every few entries

DEPLOYABLE_400.label: Capsule body plus deployable umbrella shield (beta 400)
DEPLOYABLE_400.reusable: umbrella ribs re-stow (assumed for 2226); fabric replaced every few entries

DEPLOYABLE_800.label: Capsule body plus deployable umbrella shield (beta 800)
DEPLOYABLE_800.reusable: umbrella ribs re-stow (assumed for 2226); fabric replaced every few entries

entry.packing_note: usable fraction of the bounding box: lifting body 0.45, biconic 0.55, capsule 0.50, a plain body behind a deployable shield 0.58 (authored); the deployable body is kept flat (11:4.4:3.6) to suit the mothership's slot

OPEN.label: Open rover, crew in suits
OPEN.basis: Apollo LRV 210 kg plus 2226 margin; folds

VENUS.label: Hardened pressurised rover (bathyscaphe on wheels)
VENUS.basis: computed: titanium sphere like Alvin's 2.1 m crew sphere (3 people on 10 h dives), hot-face insulation, ice heat sink, high-temperature drive; wheels beside the sphere; mates to the shuttle like a rescue submersible
VENUS.layout_note: sphere cabin slung low between four wheels; 3.6 m long so it can ride crosswise on the shuttle's lowest deck and drive out a side door

CABIN_DRIVE.label: Crew cabin drives off on its own chassis
CABIN_DRIVE.basis: SEV idea: one cabin on a wheeled chassis or a flyer; no second cabin to harden

cabin.basis: MAV cabin ~1 t/crew for a multi-day ascent; shuttle hops are hours to days (authored 0.8)

titanium.note: Ti-6Al-4V at ~735 K; thin sphere buckling P = 2E/sqrt(3(1-nu^2)) (t/R)^2 times knockdown; yield checked too

insulation.note: fibrous/aerogel blanket in hot dense CO2 (authored; gas conduction rises with pressure)

hardening.rest_note: pressure-compensated bladder tanks, high-temperature seals, SiC electronics outside the cabin (authored)

FLY_UP.label: Shuttle lands, flies up on fans, rockets from 40 km
FLY_UP.precedent: the 2024 sample-return study lifts off the surface with a high-temperature aircraft
FLY_UP.power_note: torchlet supplies electric power (Direct Fusion Drive idea); rockets without a power plant need fuel cells

BALLOON.label: Shuttle lands, balloon lifts it to 55 km, rockets from there
BALLOON.precedent: JPL metal-bellows balloon idea, called 'an extremely difficult technology element' (2024)

DROP_CITY.label: Shuttle docks at a cloud city; hardened rover drops to the surface and floats back up
DROP_CITY.precedent: Venera drag-only descent; HAVOC cloud-level crew; 2024 mid-air hand-off at ~60 km
DROP_CITY.needs: a cloud city with a capture deck (canon: Venus is a cloud civilization)

DROP_FLOAT.label: Shuttle floats on its own envelope; hardened rover drops and floats back up

geometry.note: bounding box keeps each body's proportions; packing (usable share of the box) is set per body type in entry; slot_max is the widest bay the wrap-around tanks could give up (authored)
geometry.elongation_note: stretch the body: length x e, width and height / sqrt(e); a longer, slimmer shuttle needs a longer bay but less of the mothership's cross-section

ascent_reference.note: Delta-v from the ascent simulator is computed once per world and engine for a 40 t reference shuttle, then reused in sizing; the winner is re-flown at its own mass as a check

score.note: authored weights for the single pick; feasibility (all nine jobs, aerobraking, wet mass cap) is decided first

lift_gas.note: hydrogen at ambient pressure and temperature lifts 43.45/2.016 - 1 = 20.55 kg per kg in CO2 at any height; Venus has no free oxygen, so hydrogen does not burn there

design_caps.note: authored: past ~100 t the shuttle is a second ship

refuel_ports.note: port runs: tanks topped up at a settled port before the climb (canon 2226 has settlements on all of these); expedition runs carry everything from orbit

tps_model.basis: areal TPS kg/m2 = 0.1365 * Q^0.51575 (Q in J/cm2): the Laub & Venkatapathy probe correlation turned into areal density at a probe-like beta*Cd of ~150 kg/m2, so vehicles of any density are judged per square metre of heated skin

lifting.check: Shuttle-orbiter-like case (beta ~470, 250 m2 planform) gives ~8 t, close to the orbiter's real ~9 t

deployable.check: beta 100 gives ~17 kg/m2 of umbrella, between LOFTID-class and the small ADEPT example (~26 kg/m2)
deployable.side_note: light blankets over the front 60% of a long body behind an umbrella, where the flow curling round the rim lands (authored)

tech_2226.note: 2226 baseline for finalizing: still ~40x below what Wayfarer's own torch implies per tonne (12 TW jet from a 160 t propulsion block), because small fusion drives pay a size penalty; earlier runs used 1.0

trip_payload_t.note: one drone per trip: the Mars drone or the dense-air drone
